service_name: Solid Waste Segregation Duty & Grievance Redressal
sub_service: Source segregation, door-to-door collection, bye-law penalties, grievance system
problem_type: Unsegregated waste handover, illegal dumping/littering, non-compliance with segregation duty
department: Solid Waste Management (SWM) Cell, BBMP — Head Office and Zonal levels
authority: Senior Health Inspector (Public Health Dept) / Junior Health Inspector (SWM Dept) / SWM Marshals / SWM Nodal Officer for ward
description: BBMP's Solid Waste Management Bye-laws, 2020 (notified under Sections 423, 424, 426, 431-A, 431-B of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, read with the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016) mandate every waste generator segregate waste at source into three streams: Bio-degradable/Wet (green bin), Non-biodegradable/Dry (blue bin or reusable bags), and Domestic Hazardous including Sanitary (red). BBMP deploys colour-coded collection vehicles (green=wet, blue=dry, yellow=bulk-waste) and collects wet and sanitary waste daily, dry waste at least twice or thrice weekly. The bye-laws prescribe a Schedule of Fines (Schedule VII) for non-compliance, escalating on repeat offence, and require BBMP to maintain a public grievance redressal system including the Sahaaya App/portal.
procedure: Segregate waste at source into the three mandated streams and hand it over at BBMP-notified collection times to BBMP or its Notified Service Provider (door-to-door collection). Complaints/grievances regarding non-collection of solid waste, littering, or other bye-law violations can be lodged via the Sahaaya App/portal, mobile application, complaint centre, call centre, email, or social media (WhatsApp/Twitter), per Bye-law 30(12).
sla: SLA NOT FOUND — Bye-law 30(12) states BBMP 'shall ensure that each SWM grievance is redressed in a timely and efficient manner with prescribed Service Level Agreements (SLAs) bearing in mind the type of grievance,' but the bye-law text itself does not state a specific numeric day-count SLA for a garbage-collection complaint. The only fixed, numeric norms stated are collection *frequency* (daily for wet/sanitary waste; at least 2-3 times weekly for dry waste), not a complaint-to-resolution timeline.
contact_information: A SWM Nodal Officer for ward (not below Assistant Executive Engineer rank) is appointed per ward under Bye-law 24(4). No single public phone number is stated in this document itself; complaint channels are described generically (Sahaaya App/portal, call centre, etc.) rather than with a specific number.
escalation_procedure: Spot fines/penalties for littering (Bye-law 18) and public nuisance (Bye-law 19) may be levied by: Senior Health Inspector (Public Health Dept), Junior Health Inspector (SWM Dept), SWM Marshals, or the SWM Nodal Officer for ward (Bye-law 19(5)(i)). Any Public Health/SWM official above Senior/Junior Health Inspector rank, up to Health Officer or Superintendent Engineer SWM of the Zone, is also empowered to levy spot fines (19(5)(ii)). Penalties escalate on repeat offence: the 1st offence draws the Schedule VII rate, the 2nd offence up to 2x, the 3rd up to 3x; a 4th contravention allows trade-license suspension/cancellation or legal action; grave or repeat offences can draw penalties up to Rs. 5 lakh with a police case registered (Bye-law 28). An appeal against a levied penalty goes to the Joint Commissioner of the zone, who must decide within 7 days (Bye-law 19(6)).
escalation_authority: Joint Commissioner of the zone (appellate authority for penalty disputes; 7-day disposal timeline stated)

faq.question: What happens if I hand over unsegregated (mixed) waste?
faq.answer: It is a bye-law violation subject to a fine under Schedule VII, escalating on repeat non-compliance — see Bye-law 3(2)/21.

faq.question: Who decides an appeal against a fine BBMP has levied?
faq.answer: The Joint Commissioner of the zone, who must decide the appeal within 7 days of it being filed (Bye-law 19(6)).

citizen_guidance: Segregate waste into 3 streams — green (wet/biodegradable), blue (dry/non-biodegradable), red (domestic hazardous incl. sanitary) — and hand it over at BBMP-notified collection times. Do not use plastic garbage liners. Wrap sanitary waste securely in pouches or paper before handing it over with wet waste. Non-compliance is a fineable bye-law breach, with fines escalating on repeat violation.
source_title: Solid Waste Management Bye-laws, 2020 — Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP)
